key_insight: WanPE reframes text-to-video prompting as a cinematic planning task, helping models turn a simple prompt into a director-style sequence with actions, camera movement, lighting, and sound. It uses large-scale real video data to improve how prompts guide long, multi-shot generation.
problem_solved: Modern text-to-video systems can generate longer, more complex clips, but user prompts are often too vague or underspecified to control cinematic details across a full sequence. This paper addresses the need for prompt enhancement that better specifies how scenes should unfold over time.
method: Train a 397B-parameter prompt enhancement model on 1.05M real-world videos.
Learn director-level cinematic planning from real video examples, including actions, camera trajectories, lighting, and sound cues.
Transform short user prompts into richer, production-ready prompts for long-form video generation.
impact: For practitioners, WanPE could make text-to-video generation more controllable, expressive, and reliable—especially for multi-shot or cinematic outputs. It may reduce prompt engineering effort while improving alignment between user intent and generated video structure.

paper_title: WanPE: Towards Cinematic Prompt Enhancement for Modern Text-to-Video Generation
paper_authors: Yubo Zhu, Yawen Shao, Ziyun Dai, Zixun Fang, Kai Zhu
